_comment: Machine-readable engineering baseline. Read by scripts/check-baseline.mjs and scripts/check-suppressions.mjs. Rules: docs/ENGINEERING-STANDARDS.md §1.1, §1.2, §5. Never raise a ceiling without a declaredGaps entry in the same commit.

declaredGaps.why: check:docs reads BACKTICKED document citations. The markdown-link form -- [the controls guide](./CONTROLS.md) -- is not read at all, and there are 34 of them in this repository. A gate-selftests.json entry asserted this was a REGISTERED gap; a rules audit measured that declaredGaps was empty and no row mentioned it. It is registered here because that claim was false.
declaredGaps.removal: check:docs resolves markdown-link targets, or the 34 are converted to backticks.

declaredGaps.why: check:godot and check:pixels both NOTICE and exit 0 where their tool is absent. NOTHING runs on a pull request, so before a commit reaches main the Godot half of this repository -- 13 suites, 548 assertions and the generated-data drift check -- is unenforced. Proved by a tooling audit: setting CONFIG.VERSION to 9.9.9 produced a green gate under a PATH without Godot, and the same tree failed correctly on drift the moment Godot was on PATH. A contributor who runs the gate gets a stronger check than the merge does. NARROWED, not discharged: .github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml now installs Godot 4.7.2 (pinned) and imports the project in a `verify` job that `deploy` needs, so the port IS enforced before anything is published -- but that triggers on push: main, AFTER the merge, so it cannot stop a bad commit reaching main. check:pixels still has no DISPLAY on a runner.
declaredGaps.removal: The merge path runs the gate too -- a required status check on pull requests with Godot 4.7.x installed -- so the port is enforced BEFORE the merge and not only before the publish.

declaredGaps.why: run.gd declares `evolved_before_seven_min` and achievements.gd READS it, but nothing in godot/ ever assigns it -- grep returns exactly those two hits. src/main.ts sets it when a weapon crosses its evolve level before 7 minutes, so the `early_evolve` achievement cannot fire even now that evolution is ported. Larger and related: no AchievementTracker.newly_earned call exists anywhere in godot/scripts/, so achievements are not wired into play in this slice at all.
declaredGaps.removal: A Run instance in play assigns it at the crossing, and an achievement assertion proves it fires.

declaredGaps.why: src/config.ts:53 declares `NOVA_SLOW_DEFAULT: 0.5` and NOTHING reads it -- grep returns one hit, and it is also generated into godot/data/config.gd:40 where nothing reads it either. Frost Nova uses the original's own inline `?? 0.5` / `?? 1.2` in src/weapons.ts instead. A dead constant on both sides, not a port gap.
declaredGaps.removal: Either the reader uses it, or the constant is deleted from src/data and the exporter.

declaredGaps.why: `verify_achievements.gd`'s boundary table is a HAND-WRITTEN list of 10 of the 21 achievement ids, and it omits `early_evolve` -- while `check:godot`'s own label for that suite claims "EVERY achievement is reachable and fires on its boundary". **A claim one row wider than the coverage**, which is the class AGENTS.md spends a section on. It is how `godot-early-evolve-unreachable` stayed invisible: the suite that claims to check every achievement never looked at the one that cannot fire. Found by the agent closing the volley-crit gap, measuring the adjacent claim.
declaredGaps.removal: The table is derived from the achievement registry (the way `verify_weapons` drives the real weapon table, rule 12), so a new achievement without an implemented check fails the suite -- and the gate label matches what the suite does.

declaredGaps.why: `createFloatingText` returns early TWICE in the original -- `src/main.ts:1759` `if (this.save.settings.reducedMotion) return;` and `:1763` if `damageNumbers === false` -- and neither guard has a reader in the port. `grep -rn 'damageNumbers' godot/` is 0 hits, so the field does not exist in this port's save at all, and `reducedMotion` is exactly 1 hit, the declaration at `godot/scripts/save.gd:60`, read by nothing. So the damage numbers cannot be switched off the way the original switches them off, and that is an ACCESSIBILITY regression rather than a missing convenience: `reducedMotion` exists to suppress exactly this kind of motion, and a rising, fading number is the most motion-heavy thing the port now draws.
declaredGaps.removal: `reducedMotion` is read by the floating-text sink, and `damageNumbers` exists in the port's save with an assertion that false suppresses the number and true does not.

declaredGaps.why: `grep -rn createFloatingText src/` is 11 CALL SITES in 9 groups. TWO groups are wired: `_rollCrit`'s pair (melee/instant/nova/drain) and the projectile impact at `src/main.ts:1476`. The other EIGHT draw nothing, each named rather than folded into one 'numbers are not ported': `main.ts:1366` the cold tick `#88ccff` at -36; `main.ts:1384` contact damage `#ff3333` at -30; `entities.ts:214` `'Miss!'` `#88ffcc` at -30; `:390` the bomber's blast `#ff4433` at -28; `:547` an enemy bolt `#ff6644` at -30; `:737` `OrbitShard.update` `#ffffcc` at -18 (NO crit and NO hp guard); `:777` `Mine.update` `#ff9944` at -20; `:830` an XP pickup `#66bbff` at -40. The last two are the ones a reader of `_updateProjectiles` would NOT find, because neither is in `game.projectiles`.
declaredGaps.removal: All 11 call sites have a sink, or each of the eight is declared unread with the reason it is not drawn.

declaredGaps.why: Rule 12. `godot/data/enemies.gd` carries `"bomber": true` on the Bomber row and NOTHING reads it: `grep -rn bomber godot/scripts/*.gd` returns only ARCHETYPE-STRING comparisons (`enemy.gd:192`, `game.gd:419`) plus identifiers like `_tick_bomber`. The original reads the BOOLEAN -- `src/entities.ts:338` `this.bomber = !!type.bomber`, `:376` `if (this.bomber)`, `src/entity-render.ts:222` `self.bomber && self.fuseArmed` gates the blink this work ported. **So this port's blink is gated on the archetype STRING where the original's is gated on the flag. They are the same fact today and two fields tomorrow.**
declaredGaps.removal: `enemy.gd` reads the declared `bomber` flag (or the exporter drops it), and `verify_archetypes.gd` drives the data by the flag the way `verify_weapons` drives the real weapon table.

declaredGaps.why: FOUND WHILE INTEGRATING. `scripts/lib/measurements.mjs:120` sums `/^ {2}ok {3}/` across 13 suites run with a **120 s timeout**, and sets `failed` ONLY on a `verify_X: FAIL` verdict line. **A TIMEOUT truncates with no verdict, so the total silently reads LOW and `check:claims` blames the DOCUMENT** -- the exact shape of entry 13 in `docs/PROBE-CAVEATS.md`, one level up at the measurement. CONTROL: `timeout 2 godot ... verify_slice.gd` -> 10 ok lines, NO verdict, 0 FAIL, i.e. exactly one low. Measured under load: `verify_slice` took **116.3 s against the 120 s limit**, and it is FIRST in the list, so it eats Godot's cold start. Observed live: `check:claims` read **547** once and **548** four times.
declaredGaps.removal: A truncated suite is reported as unmeasured (or the timeout is per-suite and generous), so a low total can never be mistaken for a document that disagrees.

declaredGaps.why: `_roll_crit`'s prose claims the projectile, orbit, aura and mine arms each draw ZERO crits. **Three are now pinned; the MINE arm is not.** Measured: re-adding `_roll_crit` to the mine arm leaves `verify_weapons` PASS. Projectile is pinned by the knife ratio (1.1083 vs 1.0000); aura by its draw count (0.1763 vs 0.1678); **orbit by `Shot.rolls_on_hit()`'s guard -- with the guard removed and that assertion enabled, `a shard touching 4 foes takes NO crit draw at all (0.9455 vs 0.1678)` fails, and with BOTH removed all 13 suites pass with 0 failures**, which is the evidence no pre-existing assertion covers it. This entry was first written as `godot-two-archetype-rolls-unpinned`; the FX integration closed the orbit half and a moved-base copy of the baseline silently reverted the entry, so it is recorded here in its narrowed form. **A prose claim wider than its coverage, one arm wide.**
declaredGaps.removal: The mine arm is pinned by a draw-count assertion driven from the archetype table, and the prose claim matches the number of arms actually pinned.

coverageFloors._comment: Measured coverage floors — exact values this repository achieved, not targets. They may only rise. Compared with a 0.05-point tolerance for cross-platform wobble. Refresh with: node scripts/check-coverage-floor.mjs --update

_anyCeilingNote: Raised 118 -> 137 to admit test/type-coverage.test.ts, whose FIXTURES are necessarily full of `any` — it tests the tool that counts them. Every one of the 19 added uses is a string literal fixture, not a type in shipped code. The ceiling may still only fall from here; this is a declared, bounded exception rather than a drift.
_portCeilingsRaiseNote: Raised 321 -> 323 for two commits that landed together, and the delta is FOUR top-level `const`s, not two -- this note used to name only the storage pair and read as if it paid for the whole rise. Measured per revision (the `top-level-declaration` hazard, `src/` only): fa4418e = 46, 01f25d0 = 50. The four are `STAGE_BOARD_CAP` and `MAX_TOTAL` in src/storage.ts, and `ATTR_UNSAFE` (hoisted from inside `escapeAttr`) and `CONTROL_CHARS` (new) in src/safe-html.ts. **TWO OF THE FOUR FIT THE PREVIOUS HEADROOM**: the ceiling was 321 and fa4418e measured 319, so two of the four were absorbed without a raise and the other two are what moved it to 323. All four landed in one commit, so WHICH two fitted is not attributable -- what is measured, and what this note now states, is the count at each revision and the size of the headroom. The raise is legitimate and argued on its own terms: `STAGE_BOARD_CAP` is the write path's bound, which must be the same number as the read shape's `max`, and `MAX_TOTAL` stops a cumulative total reaching `Infinity`, which `JSON.stringify` writes as `null` and the reader then refuses -- the stat silently reset to 0. `ATTR_UNSAFE` and `CONTROL_CHARS` are the two regexes the control-character XSS fix needed at module scope so `escapeAttr` and `safeUrl` share one definition each. GDScript has no variables outside a class, so all four are real port work, and all four follow the files' own existing step (`MAX_RUN_SECONDS` in src/storage.ts is declared the same way). The SILENT total is unchanged at 8, and both ceilings may still only fall.
_portCeilingsNote: Raised 319 -> 321 for the strictNullChecks work, and the reason is a real interaction rather than noise: `Number.isFinite(height)` does not narrow `number | undefined`, so the fix is an explicit `height !== undefined` check -- and `undefined` is itself a port hazard, because GDScript has only `null`. Making the code null-safe for TypeScript therefore adds sites the Godot port must rewrite. Both ceilings may still only fall, and the SILENT total is unchanged at 8.
